title: DynamoDB Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this DynamoDB course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: Which pair identifies this sample item?
options: reader and book
title and the JSON field order
exercises.explanation: A partition key chooses an item group. A sort key identifies and orders items within that group. Together they can identify one item.

exercises.question: Which attributes are declared in this table definition?
options: Every possible item field
The key attributes reader and book
exercises.explanation: A DynamoDB table declares its key attributes. Other item fields do not need to be declared as table columns.

exercises.question: What happens to an existing item at the same key?
options: PutItem replaces it unless guarded by a condition
It always creates a duplicate key
exercises.explanation: PutItem writes a complete item at its key. A later PutItem with the same key replaces the item unless a condition prevents it.

exercises.question: What key information does this GetItem need?
options: Only the pages field
Both reader and book
exercises.explanation: GetItem reads one item by its complete primary key. A missing item gives no Item field in the response.

exercises.question: What does Query require for this table?
options: A partition-key equality condition
Any random field name
exercises.explanation: Query selects one partition key and can return its related items. It is different from scanning the entire table.

exercises.question: Which field does begins_with test here?
options: Every text field in every item
The book sort key
exercises.explanation: A sort key can support a range or prefix inside one partition. begins_with keeps keys that start with the supplied text.

exercises.question: When is the full query finished?
options: When there is no LastEvaluatedKey to continue
Always after the first response
exercises.explanation: A Query response can be only one page of data. LastEvaluatedKey tells the caller where to continue.

exercises.question: Why might an existence condition be useful?
options: To sort the whole table by pages
To stop an update from creating an unintended missing item
exercises.explanation: UpdateItem can change selected attributes at a key. Expression names and values keep field names and data separate from the expression.

exercises.question: What protects the old item from replacement?
options: The attribute_not_exists condition
The title being a different string
exercises.explanation: A conditional put can require that a key does not already exist. The condition is checked as part of the write.

exercises.question: When is this filter applied?
options: Before any read work as a new key
After key-matching items are read
exercises.explanation: A FilterExpression removes items after DynamoDB reads the key-matching data. It does not make that earlier read work disappear.

exercises.question: Does TTL guarantee deletion at the exact expiry second?
options: No, deletion is asynchronous
Yes, every item vanishes at that exact instant
exercises.explanation: DynamoDB TTL uses an epoch-seconds attribute for expiry. Deletion happens later in the background, not at an exact second.

exercises.question: What limits this deletion to one item?
options: The word DELETE anywhere in the title
The complete primary key
exercises.explanation: DeleteItem targets one full key. A condition can be added when deletion must depend on the current item state.
